title: Awake's tray icon doesn't respect 24h time format
author: Rool-IO

status.label: Culture-aware Awake tray-time fix is well supported
status.detail: Awake formats its expirable tray text with a hard-coded 12-hour pattern, directly explaining why a 24-hour Windows preference still displays 1:30 instead of 13:30.

next_action.label: Design the culture-aware formatting change
next_action.reason: Queue a narrow fork-side design around the confirmed formatting call site.

judgment.rationale: The report, screenshot, and current source agree on a single mechanism: Manager.SetModeShellIcon forces `h:mm tt` rather than using the current culture's short-time pattern.
evidence: The reporter reproduces by choosing 13:30 and seeing 1:30 without an AM/PM marker.
src/modules/awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs formats ExpireAt with `MMM d, h:mm tt`.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design that replaces the forced 12-hour segment with culture-aware short-time formatting and adds 12/24-hour tests.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked upstream or fork implementation covers the confirmed hard-coded format string.

proposed_fixes.title: Respect the Windows short-time format in Awake tray text
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Manager.SetModeShellIcon hard-codes `h:mm tt`, overriding the user's 24-hour regional time preference.
plan: Extract or centralize expiration-tooltip formatting using the active culture's short-time pattern.
Replace the expirable-mode inline `h:mm tt` formatting while leaving other Awake modes unchanged.
Add focused tests for representative 24-hour and 12-hour cultures.
verification: With a 24-hour culture, an expiration at 13:30 displays 13:30.
With a 12-hour culture, the same time displays the appropriate PM marker.
Timed, indefinite, and passive tray text remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The exact symptom is generated by an exact hard-coded source format and the reporter supplied the requested visual confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Awake formats its expirable tray text with a hard-coded 12-hour pattern, directly explaining why a 24-hour Windows preference still displays 1:30 instead of 13:30.
known_information: Only the expirable tray time is described; other Awake modes are not implicated.
The current source contains an exact hard-coded 12-hour format in Manager.SetModeShellIcon.
inferences: Using CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.DateTimeFormat.ShortTimePattern should preserve both 24-hour and 12-hour user preferences.
issue_context.analysis: The code-level cause is directly visible and the correction is narrow. The later reminder adds no conflicting evidence, so a full issue-design investigation is unnecessary for this triage artifact.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, screenshot response, and latest comment.
